name: 45 Design Mouse Wheel Image Zoom
author: Tayeb Saeed

sections.description:
Explore every detail. Naturally.

Images deserve more than a quick glance. Give visitors a closer look at photography, illustrations, artwork, and other visual content with 45 Design Mouse Wheel Image Zoom.

Zoom around the mouse pointer, use a two-finger gesture on compatible touchscreens, and drag enlarged images to inspect the details that matter. Choose which images can be zoomed and adjust the experience from your WordPress dashboard.

A closer look, without replacing your gallery

45 Design Mouse Wheel Image Zoom adds configurable zoom and pan interactions to eligible WordPress images. It is designed for visual portfolios, photography websites, creative work, editorial images, and other image-rich content.

Features

  • Mouse-wheel zoom around the pointer position.
  • Two-finger zoom gestures on compatible touch devices.
  • Drag-to-pan when panning is enabled.
  • A clipping frame and constrained panning for regular page images; lightbox images follow a separate path.
  • Keyboard zoom on eligible images: focus the image, press + or – to zoom, arrows to pan when enabled, and Escape to reset.
  • Apply zoom to eligible images or individually marked images, with image/container exclusions.
  • Configure maximum zoom, zoom step, input methods, lightbox inclusion, and the reset control.
  • Handling of dynamically inserted images and reset when their loaded source changes.
  • English/Arabic Overview inside WordPress admin, with a link to Settings.

Free core plugin

The core edition is free and will remain free. A separate Pro edition is planned for the future and is not currently available.

Languages

An Arabic translation is included, and additional translations are in progress.

45 Design family

This plugin is part of the 45 Design family of WordPress plugins. It follows the family’s shared direction and works independently, without requiring another 45 Design plugin.

Gallery and lightbox compatibility

The plugin adds zoom and pan behavior; it does not replace or create a gallery or lightbox. Some third-party galleries and lightboxes may work with the plugin, but compatibility depends on their markup, styles, and gesture handling. Test your particular setup. No universal gallery compatibility is claimed.

45 Design Grid Gallery uses its own gallery/lightbox zoom and excludes those containers from this plugin to avoid competing controls. Separate page images can still use Mouse Wheel Image Zoom. Coexistence was checked with Grid Gallery 1.4.1; test your installed version.

Developed by 45 Design

Developed by Tayeb Saeed at 45 Design, Multimedia & Communication, combining visual communication experience with practical WordPress tools.

Company: https://www.45site.com/
Developer: https://www.tayebsaeed.com/
Source and issue reports: https://github.com/45-Design/Mouse-Wheel-Image-Zoom

Development and translations

An Arabic translation is included, and additional translations are in progress.
Source and issue tracking: https://github.com/45-Design/Mouse-Wheel-Image-Zoom

Optional Overview video (YouTube)

The admin Overview offers an English or Arabic introduction video according to the admin interface language. Its preview cover is served locally. No YouTube player or thumbnail is requested on page load; pressing Play explicitly loads a player from youtube-nocookie.com and requests playback. YouTube then receives the visitor network/browser information needed to provide its service. The separate Watch on YouTube link opens the video on YouTube. No image files from your galleries are sent by this feature, and public image zoom does not require the video service.

YouTube terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin and select the installable ZIP, or install the 45-design-mouse-wheel-image-zoom directory under /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate 45 Design Mouse Wheel Image Zoom.
  3. Open 45 Design Mouse Wheel Image Zoom in the admin menu below Settings. The existing entry opens Settings; choose the Overview submenu for an introduction and usage guide.
  4. Select the image scope and adjust zoom and interaction settings.
  5. Save your settings and test an eligible image on the front end, including your gallery and touch devices if used.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin improve image quality or increase resolution?

No. It enlarges the image already displayed by the browser; it does not sharpen, remove blur, upscale with AI or create missing detail. It does not automatically fetch the original-resolution attachment. Sharpness depends on the actual image source, its focus, pixel dimensions and compression.

Which images and dimensions give a better zoom experience?

Choose a sharp image with fine detail and enough pixels for its displayed size and intended zoom. For detailed photos, 2000–3000 pixels on the long edge is a useful starting point, not a required minimum or a quality guarantee. Pixel dimensions matter here, not the print DPI setting.

As a rule of thumb for each axis: source pixels ≈ displayed CSS pixels × zoom factor × device pixel ratio. For example, an image displayed 800 pixels wide needs roughly 1600 source pixels for 2× zoom on a standard-density screen, or 3200 on a 2×-density screen. This is a pixel-budget estimate, not a sharpness guarantee; raising maximum zoom cannot create source detail.

Use a good-quality, web-optimized file and balance detail against loading time. WordPress or a gallery may serve a thumbnail or smaller responsive source even when the uploaded original is large. Select a suitable image size in the editor/gallery and check the image actually loaded in the browser; this plugin scales that source rather than switching to the original. Preview the intended zoom on desktop and mobile.

Does zoom follow the pointer?

Yes. Mouse-wheel zoom uses the pointer position as its focal point, with a fresh origin after layout movement. Page-image translation is constrained by its clipping frame. Resizing the viewport resets active zoom to restore responsive layout.

Does it work on phones and tablets?

The plugin includes two-finger pinch handling for compatible touch devices. Single-finger scrolling remains native on unzoomed images. Once an image is zoomed, enabled touch/pan interaction handles the gesture. Browser and lightbox compatibility must be tested on your own devices.

Can visitors move enlarged images?

Yes, when panning is enabled. Drag the image or use arrow keys on a focused eligible image or its single-image link. Page images are constrained to their frame; lightbox layout and gestures remain dependent on the lightbox.

Does it provide keyboard-only zoom controls?

Eligible standalone images become keyboard-focusable, and single-image links use their existing focus target and show instructions on focus. Use + or – to zoom, arrows to pan when enabled, and Escape to reset. Reset zoom is also a keyboard-operable button when enabled. Single-image links keep their normal Enter behavior and do not gain an additional tab stop. Images inside buttons, editable content or links containing multiple images retain the host control’s native behavior. This does not certify complete accessibility of third-party galleries.

Can I limit zoom to selected images?

Yes. Choose “Only images individually marked for zoom”. For attachment output that uses WordPress’s image-attributes filter, enable the image’s zoom field in the Media Library. The output must retain data-mwi-attachment-zoom="1".

The WordPress attachment-image function and gallery shortcode retain this marker in tested WordPress output. Saved Gutenberg/classic image HTML and third-party renderers may omit it. For individual Gutenberg Image blocks, open block Settings → Advanced → Additional CSS class(es), add mwi-zoom (keep existing classes separated by spaces), and update the page. The class is supported on an individual figure.wp-block-image containing one image; applying it to a Group or Gallery wrapper does not select all its images. For other saved images, add mwi-zoom to the image class or add data-mwi-zoom. Changing attachment metadata alone does not rewrite saved content.

How can I exclude a logo or other image?

Apply mwi-no-zoom or data-mwi-no-zoom to the image or its container. Common .custom-logo and .avatar containers are excluded. Images with a natural width or height below 80 pixels are not eligible.

Can I change zoom strength?

Yes. Set maximum zoom from 1.5× to 10× and adjust the wheel step in Settings. Enlarging an image does not add source detail or automatically fetch the original-resolution attachment.

What happens to normal page scrolling?

Ordinary wheel gestures over eligible images control image zoom. At a zoom limit the gesture is left to the page. Ctrl/Command wheel gestures are left to the browser. Outside eligible images, scrolling remains native.

Will it work with any lightbox or gallery?

Not necessarily. Different tools intercept wheel, pointer, and touch events differently. Test the gallery you use and its lightbox inclusion setting. The plugin does not create a lightbox.

Is Arabic supported?

Arabic interface translations and a responsive RTL Overview are included. The site’s WordPress/user language determines the admin language. A focus hint explains the keyboard shortcuts in the front end’s active language.

Does it send images to an external zoom service?

The current source performs zoom in the browser on images your site supplies and includes no external zoom-service or analytics integration. Company/developer website links are provided in the admin Overview. Its optional YouTube introduction player loads only after Play is pressed; see Optional Overview video above. Other site components have their own privacy behavior.

What if zoom does not work on an image?

Confirm that zoom and the intended input method are enabled, the image is loaded and eligible, and the selected-images or exclusion rules allow it. Compare a normal page image with the gallery image. Clear relevant caches after an update, and inspect browser console errors.

Where can I get support or leave a review?

For support, email imagezoom@45site.com with WordPress/PHP versions, theme, browser/device, gallery plugin and reproduction steps. You can also report reproducible technical issues at https://github.com/45-Design/Mouse-Wheel-Image-Zoom/issues. Remove private information before sharing. Use the official WordPress.org support/review pages once the listing is confirmed available. Honest reviews are welcome; no response-time guarantee or reward is offered.
sections.changelog:
1.3.3

  • Added an English/Arabic admin Overview with dynamic version, usage guidance and links to the existing Settings page.
  • Corrected touch-pointer cleanup and disabled-input handling.
  • Preserved Boolean settings when passing configuration from WordPress to the browser.
  • Refreshed zoom origins after layout movement and reset reused image sources.
  • Added clipping and constrained pan for page images, plus focused-image keyboard zoom/pan/reset.
  • Kept reset controls outside image links and restored original inline styles and focus.
  • Corrected selected-attachment marker handling and documented WordPress output limitations.
  • Expanded PHP/browser checks and Arabic interface strings.

1.3.2

  • Fixed the missing translators comment for settings help text.
  • Removed the unnecessary manual text-domain loader for WordPress.org translation loading.
  • Clarified the read-only query checks used for the settings-saved notice.
  • Added the readme compatibility header and shortened the short description.

1.3.0

  • Added Arabic translation files and translation loading.
  • Improved settings-page styling and right-to-left layout support.
  • Preserved the 1.2.9 zoom engine to avoid introducing untested interaction changes.
  • Retained capability checks when saving per-image settings.

1.2.9

  • Restored the plugin logo in the settings-page header.
  • Added a compact plugin icon to the admin menu and positioned the menu immediately below Settings.
  • Added a Settings shortcut on the Plugins page and a successful-save notice.
  • Added an uninstall routine to remove plugin options and attachment metadata.
  • Added smooth mouse-wheel zoom animation with support for reduced-motion preferences.
  • Corrected installation and settings navigation instructions.

1.2.8

  • Temporarily removed the custom logo from the admin menu while resolving icon sizing.

1.2.7

  • Refined the admin menu icon sizing to prevent oversized display.

1.2.6

  • Updated the admin menu icon implementation during menu placement and branding refinements.

1.2.5

  • Moved the Image Zoom admin menu below Settings.
  • Refined the admin menu icon and settings-page branding.

1.2.4

  • Refined admin menu placement and plugin logo use.

1.2.3

  • Added a dedicated Image Zoom menu item in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  • Added the plugin logo to the settings screen.

1.2.2

  • Improved touch gesture handling to reduce accidental lightbox navigation after pinch zoom and panning.
  • Capture and suppress synthetic clicks following handled touch gestures.
  • Updated plugin version and asset cache version.

1.2.1

  • Improved pointer-anchored zoom calculations to reduce drift during repeated zooming.
  • Improved touch gesture handling for pinch zoom.

1.2.0

  • Added pointer-anchored mouse-wheel zoom.
  • Added touch pinch zoom and drag-to-pan support.
  • Added settings for zoom scope, maximum zoom, zoom step, input methods, lightboxes, and reset control.
  • Added image-level selection fields for WordPress media attachments and CSS class/attribute targeting.
  • Updated developer and brand details.

1.1.0

  • Added selectors for Wonder Grid Gallery and dynamically inserted lightbox images.
  • Added event-delegated mouse-wheel zoom.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with mouse-wheel image zoom.
